task.description: REWORK ITERATION 2: SECURITY-REVIEWER re-validated and FAILed again on INV-8, same invariant, narrower gap (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02c-security-reviewer.json, second FAIL). Your iteration-1 fix added `when not is_map(metadata)` as validate_metadata/1's leading guard -- but a struct IS a map in Elixir (is_map/1 returns true for structs), so it doesn't exclude them. SECURITY-REVIEWER confirmed real crashes: DateTime.utc_now() and URI.parse(...) raise Protocol.UndefinedError (no Enumerable impl); MapSet.new([1,2,3]) and 1..5 (a Range struct) raise FunctionClauseError inside validate_metadata/1's own `fn {key, value} -> ... end` since structs iterate as bare elements via Enum, not {key, value} tuples. Fix: change the guard to also reject structs, e.g. `when not is_map(metadata) or is_struct(metadata)` (a struct is never a valid metadata value here -- only a plain, non-struct map is). After fixing, do a wider sweep yourself of every place in the pre-transaction phase (P0-P6) that calls Enum.*/Map.*/String.* on caller-supplied input without first ruling out structs specifically (is_map/1 alone is not sufficient anywhere in this codebase's pattern, since every struct also satisfies it) -- check idempotency_key, payload, event_type, and any other attrs field the same way, not just metadata again. REWORK ITERATION 1: SECURITY-REVIEWER FAILed on INV-8 (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02c-security-reviewer.json). validate_metadata/1 in lib/letflow/event_store.ex (~line 233) RAISES instead of returning a typed {:error, _} on realistic malformed attrs[:metadata] input: an empty string or integer raises Protocol.UndefinedError; a non-tuple list or an atom-keyed map (e.g. %{foo: "bar"} -- an easy mistake since every other attrs key in this module is an atom) raises FunctionClauseError inside String.length/1. append/2's own @spec promises {:ok, _} | {:error, _} -- a raised exception on caller-controlled input violates that contract. Fix validate_metadata/1 (and audit the rest of the pre-transaction validation phase, P0-P6, for the same class of bug -- guard on is_map/1, is_binary/1, is_list/1 etc. before calling functions like String.length/1/Enum.count/1 that assume a specific shape) so every realistic malformed-attrs shape returns a typed {:error, {:invalid_metadata, _}}-shaped tuple (or whatever the design's error taxonomy already names) rather than raising. Add a regression check yourself (throwaway iex/mix run, not part of your committed artifacts) confirming at least: metadata as a non-map, metadata as an atom-keyed map, and metadata as a string, all now return {:error, _} rather than raising. Implement lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md's design: a new lib/letflow/event_store.ex context module (Letflow.EventStore) with append/2, per the design's Section 6 algorithm (now prose, not code -- your job is to turn that prose into real, correct Elixir/Ecto). Also add Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (the reverse of schema_name_for_tenant/1) to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, per the design's Section 4. No new migrations needed -- REQ-023 already created every table this touches. The design's OQ-5 (instance_projections insert-if-absent at first append) needs REVIEWER's explicit confirmation at Step 2d -- implement per the design's stated resolution but flag it again in your own handoff so it isn't missed.
acceptance_criteria: appending to a terminated instance (status CANCELLED or COMPLETED in instance_projections) returns an error and writes zero rows across all five involved tables, demonstrated by an actual test or iex session against a real Postgres, not just described

two concurrent appends to the same instance_id never receive the same sequence_number -- demonstrated with an actual concurrent test (e.g. Task.async_stream racing two appends) or, if concurrency can't be exercised in this environment, the FOR UPDATE-equivalent locking code path is cited explicitly
appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row, verified against the idempotency sidecar table REQ-023 defines
a payload that fails REQ-024's validate_payload/2 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections -- no partial state
a payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back after append

every row append/1(2) writes (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, the idempotency sidecar) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally -- not equal to a caller-supplied tenant_id when the two are deliberately made to disagree in a test, which must fail loudly (not silently attribute to the wrong tenant) rather than succeed

result.summary:
REWORK ITERATION 2 fix for SECURITY-REVIEWER's second INV-8 FAIL (step-02c). Root cause: iteration 1's `validate_metadata/1` leading guard was `when not is_map(metadata)` -- but in Elixir a struct IS a map (`is_map/1` returns `true` for e.g. `DateTime.utc_now()`, `URI.parse/1`'s result, `MapSet.new/1`, or a `Range` literal like `1..5`, since a struct is a map with a `:__struct__` key), so the guard never excluded them. Any struct reaching `validate_metadata/1`'s body either has no `Enumerable` impl at all (`DateTime`, `URI` -> `Protocol.UndefinedError` from `Enum.find_value/3`) or implements `Enumerable` but iterates as bare elements rather than `{key, value}` tuples (`MapSet`, `Range` -> `FunctionClauseError` inside the function's own `fn {key, value} -> ... end`), exactly as SECURITY-REVIEWER's second FAIL reproduced for all four.

Fix: changed the leading clause's guard from `when not is_map(metadata)` to `when not is_map(metadata) or is_struct(metadata)` (lib/letflow/event_store.ex, `validate_metadata/1`, ~line 256) -- both non-maps and structs now hit `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}` before `map_size/1` or `Enum.find_value/3` ever runs. Documented inline why `is_map/1` alone is insufficient, per this rework's explicit instruction that the pattern generalizes project-wide from now on.

Wider sweep of the full pre-transaction phase (P0-P6) done as instructed, not just re-patching the one line: read every field-shape guard in event_store.ex and classified each by what it actually excludes. `reject_tenant_id/1` (`Map.has_key?/2` on `attrs` itself -- structurally safe regardless of value shape, only inspects keys). `fetch_uuid/3` (instance_id/actor_id) delegates to `Ecto.UUID.cast/1`, which pattern-matches on a 36-byte dashed-hex binary or a 16-byte raw binary and falls through to a catch-all `:error` for anything else, including any struct -- structurally safe, no `is_map`-only gate involved at all. `fetch_payload/1`, `fetch_idempotency_key/1`, and `fetch_event_type/1` (added in iteration 1) all gate on `is_binary/1`, which is `false` for every struct unconditionally (a struct is never a binary) -- already safe, no change needed; iteration 1's own rhetorical claim that these were safe holds. `validate_metadata/1` was the *only* place in P0-P6 using `is_map/1` as a shape gate, so it was also the only place carrying this exact defect class -- confirmed empirically below across metadata plus 4 other fields, not just asserted from reading the code.

Verification actually run (not predicted): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exits 0 (clean, no warnings). `mix format --check-formatted` exits 0. `mix test` -- 401 tests, 4 properties, 0 failures, identical count to before this fix, full suite still green.

Regression check: wrote scratch/verify_inv8_rework2.exs (git-ignored via /scratch/, never committed), ran via `MIX_ENV=dev mix run scratch/verify_inv8_rework2.exs` against the real compiled app (docker-compose Postgres, port 5462, actually running). Confirmed by reading the `with` chain in `append/2` that none of the 5 swept fields' error paths require a provisioned tenant (all reject before `Registry.validate_payload/3`'s DB-backed `tenant_not_provisioned` check), so no tenant/schema setup was needed for the error-path assertions -- only the final control case touches the DB. Actual observed return values for all 4 of SECURITY-REVIEWER's exact struct values (`DateTime.utc_now()`, `URI.parse("http://x")`, `MapSet.new([1,2,3])`, `1..5`) against `metadata`: all 4 -> `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}`. Same 4 struct values swept against 4 other fields per the rework brief's explicit ask (wider than the minimum 2 requested): `event_type` -> all 4 `{:error, :missing_event_type}`; `idempotency_key` -> all 4 `{:error, :missing_idempotency_key}`; `instance_id` -> all 4 `{:error, :missing_instance_id}` (confirms `Ecto.UUID.cast/1` is struct-safe empirically, not just by code reading); `payload` -> all 4 `{:error, :missing_payload}`. All 4 other fields were already safe before this fix (their guards are `is_binary/1`-based, not `is_map/1`-based) -- this sweep found no additional bug beyond the one SECURITY-REVIEWER already named, and confirms it with real executed output rather than asserting it from code reading alone. Control case (well-formed metadata `%{"k" => "v"}`, all other fields valid, against a fake/unprovisioned tenant prefix) returned `{:error, :tenant_not_provisioned}` -- correctly reached the DB-backed check rather than being wrongly rejected by the tightened guard, confirming the fix doesn't over-reject well-formed input. Grep-confirmed zero `RAISED`/`THROW` lines across the entire captured output (20 struct-shaped calls + 1 control call, 0 crashes).
issues: OQ-5 (design doc §9, carried over unchanged from prior iterations, still unresolved): instance_projections insert-if-absent at first append (M6's upsert) is a real scope-boundary judgment call per the design's own framing, implemented exactly as designed -- needs REVIEWER's explicit confirmation at Step 2d, not just SECURITY-REVIEWER's tenant-isolation check.

OQ-1 (design doc §9, carried over unchanged): REQ-025's own acceptance criterion 6 names instance_sequence and event_idempotency as tables needing a correctly-derived tenant_id, but neither table carries a tenant_id column in REQ-023's shipped schema -- restated in Letflow.EventStore's moduledoc per the design's instruction; TEST-DESIGNER will need to adapt that acceptance criterion's test to a prefix-reachability check for those two tables rather than a column-value check.

OQ-4 (design doc §9, carried over unchanged from iteration 1's finding): the design assumed a malformed event_type would surface via M4's Event.insert_changeset/2 changeset, but P4 (Registry.validate_payload/3, which runs before the Multi/M4 ever opens) crashes first on any non-binary event_type. Fixed in iteration 1 via fetch_event_type/1 in event_store.ex's own pre-transaction phase; this iteration's wider sweep re-confirms fetch_event_type/1 is also struct-safe (is_binary/1-gated). REVIEWER should still confirm this divergence from OQ-4's literal text at Step 2d -- not a silent re-decision.
